original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that every nonzero algebraic number alpha that is not a root of unity satisfies a Lehmer-type lower bound for its logarithmic height?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Conjecture 4.1 (Lehmer’s Problem), specifically the equivalent height formulation stating that there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that every nonzero algebraic number α of degree at most d which is not a root of unity satisfies h(α) ≥ c/d. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly points to Lehmer’s problem, keeps the universal quantifier over nonzero algebraic numbers, excludes roots of unity, and asks for an absolute positive constant giving a uniform lower bound in terms of logarithmic height. The paper explicitly presents an equivalent formulation of Lehmer’s problem in height language. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s exact lower bound is not an unspecified 'Lehmer-type' estimate: it is precisely h(α) ≥ c/d. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))

The degree parameter d must be made explicit; in the paper it is the degree of α over Q, equivalently d = [Q(α):Q]. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))

The height is the absolute logarithmic height defined in Section 4 by h(α) = (1/d) log M(α), where M(α) is the Mahler measure of the minimal polynomial of α in Z[X]. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))

The ambient domain should be stated as all nonzero algebraic numbers α in the algebraic closure of Q, not merely algebraic integers. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))

The paper states the Mahler-measure version M(α) ≥ 1 + c as the primary formulation and then gives the height bound as an equivalent reformulation; your draft omits this exact equivalence. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))

Without the explicit c/d dependence, your wording could be read as allowing weaker bounds not intended in the paper, such as c/d^(1+ε) or other vague 'Lehmer-type' variants. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should not drift to the weaker neighboring Schinzel–Zassenhaus conjecture about the house of an algebraic integer, which the paper lists separately as Conjecture 4.2. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))
refined_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that every nonzero algebraic number α of degree d = [Q(α):Q] that is not a root of unity satisfies h(α) ≥ c/d, where h(α) = (1/d) log M(α) is the absolute logarithmic height and M(α) is the Mahler measure of the minimal polynomial of α in Z[X]? ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that every nonzero algebraic number α that is not a root of unity satisfies M(α) ≥ 1 + c, where M(α) is the Mahler measure of the minimal polynomial of α? ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))
justification: The nearest official target is Section 4.1, Conjecture 4.1, titled 'Lehmer’s Problem.' Section 4 first defines Mahler measure M(α) and logarithmic height h(α) for an algebraic number α via its minimal polynomial, and Conjecture 4.1 then states the Mahler-measure lower bound M(α) ≥ 1 + c for every nonzero non-cyclotomic algebraic number, followed immediately by the equivalent height formulation h(α) ≥ c/d for degree at most d. Your draft therefore identifies the right problem but leaves out the essential quantitative dependence on the degree and the paper’s exact definition of height. The neighboring Conjecture 4.2 is explicitly labeled weaker and concerns the house of algebraic integers, so it should not replace Conjecture 4.1. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))
